title: Sausage & Egg Breakfast Burritos
subtitle: big freezer-friendly burritos with sausage, crispy potatoes, eggs and cheddar
imageAlt: Two breakfast burritos cut in half showing scrambled egg, sausage, potatoes and melted cheddar, with mild salsa on a cream plate with a navy napkin
servingsNote: 6 big burritos: breakfast for two, plus 4 for the freezer

beforeYouStart.text: Use one big skillet for everything: sausage, potatoes, then the eggs.
Squeeze the sausage meat out of the casings.

steps.title: Par-cook
steps.text: Microwave the potatoes in a covered bowl with 2 tbsp water 4–5 minutes, until just tender. Drain.

steps.title: Sausage
steps.text: Brown the sausage meat in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high, breaking it up, 8–10 minutes, until no pink remains and it reads 71°C (160°F). Lift it out with a slotted spoon.

steps.title: Potatoes
steps.text: Add the oil and potatoes to the pan and cook 6–8 minutes, turning, until golden. Season with paprika and salt and add to the sausage.

steps.title: Eggs
steps.text: Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper. Melt the butter in the pan over medium-low and stir the eggs gently 3–4 minutes, until firm with no runny egg left.

steps.title: Roll
steps.text: Warm the tortillas 20 seconds in the microwave. Fill each with eggs, sausage and potatoes, cheddar and a spoon of salsa. Fold in the sides and roll up tight.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Toast them seam side down in the dry skillet over medium 1–2 minutes a side, until golden.

fixIt.fix: Cool the filling completely before rolling, and keep the salsa to a spoon each.
Warm them first so they fold without splitting.
Lower heat and take them off as soon as they're firm.

saleTip: Mild Italian sausage at No Frills often drops to $5.99 for 500 g; any mild pork sausage works.
swap: Ground pork with ½ tsp each salt and dried sage for sausage. Frozen diced hash browns for potatoes.
leftovers: Wrap each in foil and freeze in a bag; grab one on the way out the door.
doneness: Sausage meat to 71°C (160°F) (Health Canada, ground pork); eggs cooked until firm; reheat burritos to 74°C (165°F).
source: Based on tested freezer breakfast burrito methods (Budget Bytes, Canadian Living): browned sausage, pan-crisped potatoes and soft scrambled eggs rolled with cheddar and toasted.
prepAhead: Cook the sausage and potatoes up to 2 days ahead.
Freeze rolled burritos up to 3 months.
reheat: From frozen: unwrap, wrap in a paper towel and microwave 2–3 minutes, turning halfway, until 74°C (165°F) in the centre.
airFryer: To crisp frozen burritos: air-fry at 180°C (350°F) for 12–15 minutes, turning once, until 74°C (165°F) in the centre. Fresh ones need only 4–5 minutes instead of the skillet.

basic.note: Sausage, egg and cheese burritos; no potatoes or salsa.

fancy.note: Avocado and sour cream tucked inside each one.

stepNotes.4: Fancy: add avocado and a spoon of sour cream before rolling (eat these fresh; avocado doesn't freeze well).

plating: Cut on a sharp angle to show the filling.
Salsa and sour cream in small dishes.

why.0-0: Par-cooking the potatoes gets them crisp in minutes.
why.2-0: Large tortillas leave room to fold the ends in so nothing leaks.

funFact: The breakfast burrito is usually traced to Tia Sophia's restaurant in Santa Fe, New Mexico, which put it on the menu in the 1970s.
drink: Coffee, or a glass of cold orange juice.
